results.title: Experts On Demand – Edmonton Unlimited
results.content: **Experts on Demand (EOD)** is a milestone-driven program connecting growth-stage companies in the Edmonton Region with specialized industry experts, providing up to 100 hours of fractional support. Together, founders and experts collaborate to tackle specific challenges, drive measurable growth, and expand businesses through tangible deliverables. After a rigorous qualification process assessing your growth potential, you’ll work with Edmonton Unlimited to engage an expert aligned with your specific needs. Together, you’ll develop a structured project with clear milestones, measurable outcomes, and regular check-ins to ensure progress. The expert will provide fractional support by developing specific deliverables while transferring knowledge to build your team’s capacity. * **Milestone-Driven Implementation**: Projects follow structured frameworks with clear sprints, specific milestones, and measurable outcomes to ensure tangible business value and track progress effectively. * **Enhanced Expert Qualification**: Experts undergo rigorous vetting for their proven ability to drive business results and are onboarded with our venture development methodology to ensure consistent, high-quality delivery. * **Impact Measurement System**: All projects include comprehensive accountability mechanisms to measure expert contributions and business outcomes, ensuring execution viability and meaningful ROI within project budget ranges. * **Replacement Work**: Projects where experts simply perform ongoing operational functions instead of building your team’s capacity to handle these functions independently. * **Expert Engagement & Scoping**: Work with Edmonton Unlimited to engage an expert and collaborate on defining clear project scope, deliverables, milestones, and success metrics. * **Project Implementation**: Engage in regular check-ins and capacity-building sessions as your expert delivers tangible outcomes while transferring knowledge to your team. * **Impact Measurement & Continuous Support**: Track and validate project outcomes against established metrics with ongoing support to maintain momentum toward critical business milestones. As an expert with proven ability to drive tangible business results and a willingness to give back to the community, you can provide one-on-one support to help businesses grow. This program is offered at no cost, thanks to Alberta Innovates, through the Edmonton Regional Innovation Network, along with Prairies Economic Development Canada. The Student Innovation Centre within the Faculty of Science at the University of Alberta and Edmonton Unlimited are working together to help bring your big ideas to life.

results.title: What to Look for in the New York City Fiscal Year 2026 Preliminary Budget |
results.content: # What to Look for in the New York City Fiscal Year 2026 Preliminary Budget. The State and City Comptrollers, Independent Budget Office (IBO), and City Council all recently updated their revenue forecasts for fiscal years 2025 and 2026 to recognize billions of additional tax dollars. When Mayor Adams delivers the Fiscal Year 2026 Preliminary Budget, the Citizens Budget Commission (CBC) will identify if the City provides accurate and reasonable estimates of future revenues and expenses and takes the necessary steps to ensure spending is affordable in fiscal year 2026 and beyond. Of this, nearly $1 billion are operating costs that should be reflected in the Preliminary Budget; the remaining City costs should be reflected in the Preliminary Capital Commitment Plan.2 Mayor Adams’ proposal to eliminate the NYC Personal Income Tax for some low-income New Yorkers is expected to cost $63 million.3 Other new initiatives, such as $650 million to address street homelessness and $163 million to serve at-risk youth announced during the State of the City, should be funded in the budget as well.4. How, besides increased revenue, does the City close the fiscal year 2026 gap?**The Preliminary Budget is required by law to be balanced in fiscal years 2025 and 2026. First, the City has $1.45 billion of in-year budgetary reserves in fiscal year 2025 to help close future budget gaps if this money is not needed to fund underbudgeted expenses in fiscal year 2025. How large are the City’s out-year budget gaps and are they increased by new spending?**The November Plan reports budget gaps totaling $5.6 billion in fiscal year 2027 and $6.3 billion in fiscal year 2028, although the gaps exceed $8 billion annually after accounting for underbudgeting. 5. According to the City Comptroller, “Under the City’s accrual method of budgeting, when prior year expenses are taken down in a closed fiscal year they are recognized as savings in the current year.” Office of the New York City Comptroller, *Annual State of the City’s Economy and Finances* (December 2024), p.
